data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Navigation often assumes stable physical laws (uniformity), whereas Popper explicitly denies assuming natural uniformity","Medical triage usually relies on statistical probability of survival, which Popper rejects as a basis for theory choice"],"overturn_conditions":["If it is shown that navigating by star charts logically implies a belief that stars will remain in place (induction), then the analogy fails to support non-inductive action","If medical triage cannot be conducted without implicit probabilistic assumptions, then the analogy smuggles in the very thing Popper rejects"],"shared_structure":["Decision made under conditions where positive prediction is impossible","Preference given to the option with the most rigorous historical stress-testing","Goal is optimization of process (learning/survival) rather than guarantee of outcome"],"source_memory_refs":["navIGATION_by_star_position_despite_uncertainty","medical_triage_based_on_survival_rates_not_cure_guarantees"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a navigator uses the most verified star charts without claiming they guarantee safe passage, a Popperian scientist uses the best-corroborated theory without claiming it guarantees predictive success","The rationality lies in the selection procedure (using the best available data), not in the expected result"]},"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible without smuggling in induction by framing it as a non-epistemic, methodological rule of 'critical rationality': we prefer the theory that has withstood the severest tests not because it is more likely to be true or successful in the future, but because it is the most informative theory currently available for criticism and error elimination. The cost of this view is the abandonment of any rational expectation that the future will resemble the past; action becomes a gamble on the best-tested error-correcting mechanism rather than a prediction based on accumulated probability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If one can demonstrate that acting on a theory logically entails an assumption that its past success predicts future success, then the preference smuggles in induction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Popper's own examples of 'acting' on theories implicitly rely on a principle of uniformity of nature that he explicitly denies, then his position is inconsistent.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the concept of 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) is required to justify the preference but remains formally undefined or incoherent for false theories, then the defense collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reinterpret 'preference' not as an inductive inference about future truth (which Popper rejects) but as a procedural commitment to the theory with the highest empirical content and testability. Since high corroboration implies a theory has survived severe attempts to falsify its high-content claims, choosing it maximizes the potential for learning (error detection) regardless of whether it turns out to be true. This aligns with Popper's distinction between the logical status of a theory (unchanged by testing) and the pragmatic decision of which theory to subject to further critical scrutiny.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
